items.title: DSFlow: A Neuro-Symbolic Data Workflow Agent with Statistical Diagnostic Guardrails
items.description: arXiv:2611.25111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data science workflows often require tools that presume non-trivial technical knowledge. Large language models (LLMs) reduce this barrier, but a gap remains between flexible general-purpose agents and statistically controlled pipelines. We introduce DSFlow, a LangGraph-based neuro-symbolic data-agent platform that combines reusable, LLM-selected skills with deterministic diagnostic guardrails. Skills provide extensible task knowledge. Symbolic validation can accept a proposed method, request clarification or replanning, override an unsuitable method, or supply a safe fallback. Regression and clustering case studies illustrate how DSFlow uses diagnostic evidence to correct method choices and documents those decisions in auditable reports.

items.description: arXiv:2611.25325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Present artificial intelligence agents are constructed by means of a coupling between a fixed language model with a general computing device. items.description: arXiv:2611.25393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems replicate through deployment, vary through training, and compete for computational resources.
